headline: One month on: 3 deaths, 4,633 homes destroyed among 19,865 evaluated, and 62,665 people affected; 2,731 remain in 100 shelters. Reconstruction has started (300+ homes under way) but is slow, and aftershocks continue, including an M5.9 near Tonosí on 31 Oct.
key_points: Official: 3 deaths (third on 30 Oct), 27 injured; 62,665 people affected (SINAPROC, 8 Nov); 2,731 people in 100 shelters, down from 6,654 at the peak.
Homes (COE, 2 Nov): 19,865 evaluated: 4,633 total damage, 11,107 moderate or partial, 4,125 minor. Veraguas alone has 2,179 destroyed; Tonosí ~110 to demolish.
Reconstruction: 311 homes in demolition or construction; 3,500 housing solutions planned, replacement homes due by 31 March 2027; 1,200 local jobs; families say progress is slow.
Money: under US$20M of the US$100M emergency trust disbursed, requests near US$80M; Government says reconstruction has 'no fiscal ceiling'. Insurers: 6,453 claims, B/.108.7M reserved.
Schools: 1,342 of 2,000 inspected operating; demolition of collapsed schools under way; UNICEF says 90,000 students affected.
Aftershocks: 1,483 so far, rate down ~80%; M5.8 and M5.9 near Tonosí on 31 Oct and M5.0 on 6 Nov, no new casualties; 12,251 landslides mapped.
Colón: 200+ families from cracked downtown buildings to be relocated to Alto de los Lagos in Nov–Dec.
Preparedness: Government will fund an earthquake early-warning system (US$1.5–3M); USGS sending fault specialists.

areas.area: Los Santos (Macaracas, Tonosí, Las Tablas, Pedasí)
areas.text: 4,633 homes destroyed nationally, most in Los Santos and Herrera. Tonosí: 1,600+ structures affected, ~110 homes to demolish, Búcaro road offset ~2 m, modular hospital site prepared; M5.8–5.9 aftershocks on 31 Oct cut power in Cañas. Isla Cañas families still displaced.

areas.area: Herrera (Los Pozos, Las Minas, Pesé, Ocú)
areas.text: Large share of destroyed homes and 20 of the 35 collapsed schools (Las Minas, Los Pozos). First 300 government homes under way; US Embassy delivered modular homes in El Rincón.

2,179 homes destroyed, mainly in Mariato and Soná; 1,635 people still in shelters (largest share); first rebuilt home delivered in Quebrada Grande (Soná); 80+ schools need repair, six bridges affected; some Soná communities still cut off.
Penonomé cathedral and governorship damaged; demolition of quake-damaged schools started (Sagrejá, San Isidro, El Potrero); 67 homes in reconstruction; most shelters closed.
Eastern Chiriquí and Ngäbe-Buglé: mostly adobe homes damaged; 85 homes in reconstruction in Chiriquí; 27 schools in Bocas del Toro, Chiriquí and Ngäbe-Buglé reopen on 11 Nov.

Policlínica Presidente Remón still closed; Metro, Tocumen and ports normal. Colón: 200+ families from cracked downtown buildings to be relocated. M3.9 on the Pedro Miguel fault (4 Nov) briefly evacuated the Metro, unrelated to Azuero.

services.text: 19,865 evaluated, 4,633 destroyed (2 Nov); 2,731 people in 100 shelters; 311 homes in demolition or construction; replacement homes due 31 March 2027.
1,342 of 2,000 inspected schools operating; demolitions under way; 85 schools to rebuild for March 2027; 27 more schools reopen 11 Nov.
MINSA: 15 hospitals at 100%, 118 facilities pending repair; CSS: Remón, Los Pozos and Tonosí closed or in modular units; modular hospital planned in Tonosí.
70 damaged roads cleared, work on 29 fronts; Búcaro road needs redesign; MOP repair cost not yet published.
Power and water largely restored; Cañas briefly lost power after the 31 Oct aftershocks; water shortages persist in parts of Veraguas.
Tocumen and Metro Lines 1 and 2 operating since 12 Oct; state ports back to ~80%.

upcoming: Coming up: MOP road and bridge costs; MICI business-damage report to Cabinet; possible increase of the US$100M emergency allocation; Moody's rating review in November.
unknowns: How many homes will need full replacement: COE counts 4,633 destroyed, MIVIOT 5,871 total loss and 40,720 with some damage.
Total cost of damage: MEF requests near US$80M; MOP road and bridge costs and private losses not yet included.
Where Isla Cañas residents will be relocated.
How many of the planned homes will be finished before the March 2027 deadline.
